# Developer Guidance — Backend / CLI (Node + TypeScript)

## Standard scripts

Your `package.json` must define these scripts exactly:

```json
"scripts": {
  "dev":       "tsx watch src/index.ts",
  "build":     "tsc",
  "start":     "node dist/index.js",
  "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
  "lint":      "oxlint src"
}
```

`tsx` is the development runner — fast startup, no type-checking overhead. Type correctness is enforced separately via `npm run typecheck`.

## When to run each command

| Situation | Command |
|-----------|---------|
| After any structural change (new file, moved import, changed interface) | `npm run typecheck` |
| Before committing | `npm run typecheck` then `npm run lint` — both must pass with zero errors |
| Before opening a PR | `npm run build` — must complete without errors |
| Verifying runtime behaviour | `npm run dev`, then test manually or run your test suite |

## Type-checking test files co-located in src/

When test files (`*.test.ts`) or fixture suites (`__fixtures__/`) live under `src/` and are
excluded from the production `tsconfig.json`, `tsc --build` will not type-check them. Add a
second `noEmit` pass that uses a separate `tsconfig.test.json`:

```json
"compile": "tsc --build && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json"
```

`tsconfig.test.json` extends the base config and overrides two things:

```json
{
  "extends": "./tsconfig.json",
  "compilerOptions": { "composite": false, "noEmit": true },
  "include": ["src/**/*.ts"],
  "exclude": ["**/*.test.integration.ts"]
}
```

The key difference from the base `exclude`: it does **not** list `**/*.test.ts` or
`**/__fixtures__/**`, so those files are type-checked here even though they are excluded from
the production emit. This catches type errors in test and fixture code without polluting `dist/`.

## WSL (if used)

WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) lets you run a Linux environment on Windows. If you are developing inside WSL, do **not** work from `/mnt/c/...` — npm will pick up the Windows `.npmrc` and fail. Always open a terminal from the WSL-native path (e.g. `~/projects/...`).

## Common pitfalls

- **Using `any`** — TypeScript strict mode is on; use discriminated unions or `unknown` with narrowing instead
- **Importing with `.js` extensions for local files** — only add `.js` if your `tsconfig.json` targets ESM with `"moduleResolution": "bundler"` or `"node16"`; check the project config first
- **Running `npm run build` as a type-check** — use `npm run typecheck` instead; `build` emits compiled output to `dist/` which is unnecessary mid-development
- **Running the compiled output during development** — use `npm run dev` (tsx watch), not `npm start`, to pick up changes without a rebuild
